rows.extract: My Lover, My Son is a 1970 American-British coproduction drama film directed by John Newland. It tells the story of a mother played by Romy Schneider clinging to her maturing son. The film is based on Edward Grierson's 1952 novel Reputation for a Song.

rows.cast: Nigel Davenport, Jean Wallace, Lynne Frederick

rows.title: Norwood

rows.cast: Sammy Davis Jr., Peter Lawford, Esther Anderson

rows.cast: Jack Wild, Billie Hayes, Martha Raye
rows.extract: Pufnstuf is a 1970 American comedy fantasy musical film produced by Sid and Marty Krofft Enterprises and released by Universal Pictures. It is based on the children's television series H.R. Pufnstuf, a show that features a cast of puppets on a "living island."

rows.extract: Night Call Nurses is a 1972 American sex comedy film directed by Jonathan Kaplan. It is the third in Roger Corman's "nurses" cycle of films, starting with The Student Nurses (1970).

rows.title: No Drums, No Bugles
rows.cast: Martin Sheen, Davey Davison
rows.extract: No Drums, No Bugles is a 1972 American drama film written, produced and directed by Clyde Ware. The film stars Martin Sheen, Davey Davison, Rod McCary and Denine Terry. The film was released on February 23, 1972, by Cinerama Releasing Corporation.

rows.title: No Place to Run
rows.cast: Herschel Bernardi, Stefanie Powers, Larry Hagman
rows.extract: No Place to Run is a 1972 American made-for-television drama film directed by Delbert Mann and starring Herschel Bernardi, Stefanie Powers and Larry Hagman.

rows.cast: Anita Ekberg, John Ireland, Victor Buono
rows.extract: Northeast of Seoul is a 1972 American action-thriller film directed by David Lowell Rich. It stars Anita Ekberg and John Ireland, with music by Alan Heyman.

rows.extract: The Offence is a 1973 British crime neo noir drama film directed by Sidney Lumet, based upon the 1968 stage play This Story of Yours by John Hopkins. rows.title: One Is a Lonely Number
rows.cast: Trish Van Devere, Monte Markham, Janet Leigh
rows.extract: One Is a Lonely Number is a 1972 American drama film directed by Mel Stuart, and starring Trish Van Devere, Janet Leigh, and Melvyn Douglas. The screenplay, based upon the short story "The Good Humor Man" by Rebecca Morris, was written by David Seltzer.

rows.title: The Other
rows.cast: Uta Hagen, Diana Muldaur, John Ritter
rows.extract: The Other is a 1972 American horror psychological thriller film directed by Robert Mulligan, adapted for film by Thomas Tryon from his 1971 novel of the same name. rows.extract: Painters Painting: The New York Art Scene 1940-1970 is a 1972 documentary directed by Emile de Antonio. rows.title: Pete 'n' Tillie
rows.cast: Walter Matthau, Carol Burnett, Geraldine Page
rows.extract: Pete 'n' Tillie is a 1972 American comedy-drama film directed by Martin Ritt and starring Walter Matthau and Carol Burnett. Its advertising tagline was: "Honeymoon's over. It's time to get married."

rows.title: Pickup on 101
rows.cast: Jack Albertson, Lesley Ann Warren, Martin Sheen
rows.extract: Pickup on 101 is a 1972 American drama film directed by John Florea and written by Anthony Blake. The film stars Jack Albertson, Lesley Ann Warren, Martin Sheen, Hal Baylor, George Chandler and Robert Donner. The film was released in May 1972, by American International Pictures.

rows.cast: Divine
rows.extract: Pink Flamingos is a 1972 American black comedy film directed, written, produced, narrated, filmed, and edited by John Waters. rows.title: Play It Again, Sam
rows.cast: Woody Allen, Diane Keaton, Tony Roberts, Susan Anspach
rows.extract: Play It Again, Sam is a 1972 American comedy film written by and starring Woody Allen, based on his 1969 Broadway play of the same name. The film was directed by Herbert Ross, instead of Allen, who usually directs his own written work.

rows.title: Play It as It Lays
rows.cast: Tuesday Weld, Anthony Perkins, Adam Roarke
rows.extract: Play It As It Lays is a 1972 American drama film directed by Frank Perry and written by Joan Didion and John Gregory Dunne, based on the novel of the same name by Didion. The film stars Tuesday Weld and Anthony Perkins, who previously starred together in the 1968 film Pretty Poison.

rows.title: Pocket Money
rows.cast: Paul Newman, Lee Marvin
rows.extract: Pocket Money is a 1972 American Western buddy comedy film directed by Stuart Rosenberg, from a screenplay written by Terrence Malick and based on the 1970 novel Jim Kane by J.P.S. Brown. The film stars Paul Newman and Lee Marvin and takes place in 1970s Arizona and northern Mexico.

rows.title: Pope Joan
rows.cast: Liv Ullmann, Olivia de Havilland
rows.extract: Pope Joan is a 1972 British historical drama film based on the story of Pope Joan. Even though modern consensus generally considers Pope Joan to be legendary, in the film her existence is treated as fact.

rows.title: Portnoy's Complaint
rows.cast: Richard Benjamin, Karen Black, Lee Grant
rows.extract: Portnoy's Complaint is a 1972 American comedy film written and directed by Ernest Lehman. His screenplay is based on the bestselling 1969 novel of the same name by Philip Roth.

rows.title: One Little Indian

rows.title: Act of Vengeance

rows.extract: Act of Vengeance, also known as Rape Squad and The Violator, is a 1974 American exploitation film. It was directed by Bob Kelljan and stars Jo Ann Harris, Peter Brown, Jennifer Lee, Connie Strickland, Lisa Moore, Tony Young, Steve Kanaly and Anneka Di Lorenzo.

rows.title: Airport 1975
rows.cast: Charlton Heston, Karen Black, Gloria Swanson, Linda Blair, George Kennedy
rows.extract: Airport 1975 is a 1974 American air disaster film and the first sequel to the successful 1970 film Airport. It was directed by Jack Smight, produced by William Frye, executive produced by Jennings Lang, and written by Don Ingalls. The film stars Charlton Heston, Karen Black, George Kennedy and Glori

rows.title: Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore
rows.cast: Ellen Burstyn, Kris Kristofferson, Diane Ladd, Harvey Keitel, Valerie Curtin
rows.extract: Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore is a 1974 American comedy drama film directed by Martin Scorsese and written by Robert Getchell. It stars Ellen Burstyn as a widow who travels with her preteen son across the Southwestern United States in search of a better life. Kris Kristofferson, Billy "Green" Bush

rows.title: Amazing Grace
rows.cast: Moms Mabley, Slappy White, Rosalind Cash
rows.extract: Amazing Grace is a 1974 American comedy film directed by Stan Lathan and starring Moms Mabley and Moses Gunn. The film's title is a play on words based on the name of the Christian hymn "Amazing Grace".

rows.title: The Arena
rows.cast: Pam Grier, Margaret Markov, Paul Muller (actor)
rows.extract: The Arena, also known as Naked Warriors, is a 1974 gladiator exploitation film directed by Steve Carver and starring Margaret Markov and Pam Grier. Joe D'Amato, the film's cinematographer, has stated that he took over direction of the fight scenes in the film.

rows.title: Bad Ronald
rows.cast: Scott Jacoby, Pippa Scott, John Larch, Dabney Coleman, Kim Hunter
rows.extract: Bad Ronald is a 1974 American made-for-television horror thriller film directed by Buzz Kulik and starring Scott Jacoby, Pippa Scott, John Larch, Dabney Coleman and Kim Hunter. It is based on the novel of the same title by Jack Vance.

rows.title: Bank Shot
rows.cast: George C. Scott, Joanna Cassidy, Sorrell Booke
rows.extract: Bank Shot is a 1974 heist film directed by Gower Champion and written by Wendell Mayes. It was loosely based upon Donald E. Westlake's 1972 novel of the same name, which was the second book of his "Dortmunder" series. The film stars George C. Scott, Joanna Cassidy, Sorrell Booke, and G. Wood.

rows.title: The Bat People
rows.cast: Stewart Moss, Marianne McAndrew, Michael Pataki
rows.extract: The Bat People is a 1974 American horror film directed by Jerry Jameson, written and produced by Lou Shaw, and distributed by American International Pictures. Starring Stewart Moss and Marianne McAndrew, the film tells the story of a doctor, who after being bitten by a bat in a cave, undergoes an ac

rows.title: The Bears and I
rows.cast: Patrick Wayne, Chief Dan George, Andrew Duggan
rows.extract: The Bears and I is a 1974 American drama film directed by Bernard McEveety and written by John Whedon. The film stars Patrick Wayne, Chief Dan George, Andrew Duggan, Michael Ansara and Robert Pine. The film was released on July 31, 1974, by Buena Vista Distribution.

rows.title: Benji
rows.cast: Patsy Garrett, Christopher Connelly, Patsy Garrett, Peter Breck
rows.extract: Benji is a 1974 American family film written, produced and directed by Joe Camp. It is the first in a series of five films about the golden mixed breed dog named Benji. Filmed in and around McKinney and Denton in Texas, the story follows Benji, a stray but friendly dog, who is adored by some of the

rows.title: Beyond the Door
rows.cast: Juliet Mills, Richard Johnson, Gabriele Lavia
rows.extract: Beyond the Door is a 1974 supernatural horror film directed by Ovidio G. Assonitis and Roberto Piazzoli, and starring Juliet Mills, Gabriele Lavia, and Richard Johnson. The plot follows a San Francisco housewife who becomes demonically possessed in the midst of a pregnancy. The film was a co-product

rows.title: Big Bad Mama
rows.cast: Angie Dickinson, William Shatner, Tom Skerritt
rows.extract: Big Bad Mama is a 1974 American action-crime-sexploitation comedy movie produced by Roger Corman, starring Angie Dickinson, William Shatner, and Tom Skerritt, with Susan Sennett and Robbie Lee. This movie is about a mother, Wilma, and her two daughters, Polly and Billie Jean, who go on a crime spree

rows.title: Billy Two Hats
rows.cast: Gregory Peck, Desi Arnaz Jr., Jack Warden
rows.extract: Billy Two Hats is a 1974 American Western film directed by Ted Kotcheff. It stars Gregory Peck, Jack Warden and Desi Arnaz, Jr.

rows.title: Black Belt Jones
rows.cast: Jim Kelly, Gloria Hendry, Eric Laneuville
rows.extract: Black Belt Jones is a 1974 American blaxploitation martial arts film directed by Robert Clouse and starring Jim Kelly and Gloria Hendry. The film is a spiritual successor to Clouse's prior film Enter the Dragon, in which Kelly had a supporting role. Here, Kelly features in his first starring role as

rows.title: Black Eye
rows.cast: Fred Williamson, Rosemary Forsyth, Teresa Graves
rows.extract: Black Eye is a 1974 American neo-noir action and blaxploitation film produced by Pat Rooney, directed by Jack Arnold and starring Fred Williamson. The film was based on the 1971 novel Murder on the Wild Side by Jeff Jacks.

rows.title: The Black Godfather
rows.cast: Rod Perry, Don Chastain, Jimmy Witherspoon
rows.extract: The Black Godfather is a 1974 American blaxploitation film written and directed by John Evans and starring Rod Perry, Don Chastain, Diane Sommerfield and Jimmy Witherspoon. The plot is about J.J., a rising star in the black crime scene, who is in the process of consolidating his power over the neigh

rows.title: Black Samson
rows.cast: Rockne Tarkington, William Smith, Carol Speed
rows.extract: Black Samson is a 1974 American blaxploitation film, starring Rockne Tarkington, Carol Speed, William Smith and Connie Strickland. The film was written by Daniel B. Cady and Warren Hamilton Jr., directed by Charles Bail and released by Warner Bros. It was the directorial debut for Bail, more commonl

rows.title: Blazing Saddles
rows.cast: Cleavon Little, Gene Wilder, Mel Brooks, Madeline Kahn, Harvey Korman
rows.extract: Blazing Saddles is a 1974 American satirical western black comedy film directed by Mel Brooks, who co-wrote the screenplay with Andrew Bergman, Richard Pryor, Norman Steinberg and Alan Uger, based on a story treatment by Bergman. The film stars Cleavon Little and Gene Wilder. The film received gener

rows.title: Bootleggers
rows.cast: Paul Koslo, Jaclyn Smith, Slim Pickens
rows.extract: Bootleggers is a 1974 American comedy-drama film directed by Charles B. Pierce and starring Paul Koslo and Dennis Fimple.

rows.title: Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia
rows.cast: Warren Oates, Isela Vega, Helmut Dantine, Robert Webber, Emilio Fernandez
rows.extract: Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia is a 1974 Mexican-American neo-Western film directed by Sam Peckinpah, co-written by Peckinpah and Gordon Dawson from a story by Peckinpah and Frank Kowalski, and starring Warren Oates and Isela Vega, with Robert Webber, Gig Young, Helmut Dantine, Emilio Fernández

rows.title: Buster and Billie
rows.cast: Jan-Michael Vincent, Pamela Sue Martin, Clifton James, Robert Englund, Joan Goodfellow
rows.extract: Buster and Billie is a 1974 American neo noir crime film motion picture released by Columbia Pictures. The film was of the tragic romance/revenge film genres. It was directed by Daniel Petrie, whose credits include films such as Fort Apache, The Bronx (1981).

rows.title: Busting
rows.cast: Elliott Gould, Robert Blake, Allen Garfield
rows.extract: Busting is a 1974 American crime film directed by Peter Hyams in his theatrical directorial debut, starring Elliott Gould and Robert Blake as Los Angeles police detectives. It was the main inspiration for the cop series Starsky & Hutch, which premiered in 1975 and, like this film, also featured Anto

rows.title: Caged Heat
rows.cast: Erica Gavin, Roberta Collins, Barbara Steele
rows.extract: Caged Heat, also known as Renegade Girls, is a 1974 women in prison film. It was written and directed by Jonathan Demme for New World Pictures, headed by Roger Corman. The film stars Juanita Brown, Roberta Collins, Erica Gavin, Ella Reid, Rainbeaux Smith, and Barbara Steele.

rows.title: The California Kid
rows.cast: Martin Sheen
rows.extract: The California Kid is a 1974 American made-for-television action thriller film directed by Richard T. Heffron and starring Martin Sheen.

rows.title: California Split
rows.cast: Elliott Gould, George Segal, Ann Prentiss
rows.extract: California Split is a 1974 American comedy-drama film directed by Robert Altman and starring Elliott Gould and George Segal as a pair of gamblers and was the first non-Cinerama film to use eight-track stereo sound.

rows.title: The Castaway Cowboy
rows.cast: James Garner, Vera Miles, Eric Shea, Robert Culp
rows.extract: The Castaway Cowboy is a 1974 American comedy western film released by Walt Disney Productions starring James Garner, Vera Miles, Eric Shea, and Robert Culp about a Texas rancher who gets shanghaied, then jumps ship and finds himself washed ashore in Hawaii. Filmed on location in Hawaii, the film wa

rows.title: Catch My Soul
rows.cast: Richie Havens, Lance LeGault, Season Hubley
rows.extract: Catch My Soul is a 1974 film produced by Jack Good and Richard M. Rosenbloom, and directed by Patrick McGoohan. It was an adaptation of Good's stage musical of the same title, which itself was loosely adapted from William Shakespeare's Othello. It was not a critical success.

rows.title: Chinatown
rows.cast: Jack Nicholson, Faye Dunaway, John Huston, Perry Lopez, Diane Ladd
rows.extract: Chinatown is a 1974 American neo-noir mystery film directed by Roman Polanski from a screenplay by Robert Towne, starring Jack Nicholson and Faye Dunaway. The film was inspired by the California water wars, a series of disputes over southern California water at the beginning of the 20th century, by

rows.title: Chosen Survivors
rows.cast: Diana Muldaur, Bradford Dillman, Jackie Cooper
rows.extract: Chosen Survivors is a 1974 Mexican-American horror science fiction film directed by Sutton Roley and starring Jackie Cooper, Alex Cord, Richard Jaeckel, Bradford Dillman, Pedro Armendáriz Jr. and Diana Muldaur

rows.title: Claudine
rows.cast: Diahann Carroll, James Earl Jones, Lawrence Hilton-Jacobs
rows.extract: Claudine is a 1974 American romantic comedy-drama film, directed by John Berry. Claudine was written by Lester Pine and Tina Pine, produced by Third World Cinema, and distributed by 20th Century Fox, starring James Earl Jones, Diahann Carroll, and Lawrence Hilton-Jacobs. The film was released on Apr

rows.title: Cockfighter
rows.cast: Warren Oates, Harry Dean Stanton, Ed Begley Jr.
rows.extract: Cockfighter is a 1974 drama film by director Monte Hellman, starring Warren Oates, Harry Dean Stanton and featuring Laurie Bird and Ed Begley, Jr. The screenplay is based on the 1962 novel of the same title by Charles Willeford.

rows.title: Conrack
rows.cast: Jon Voight, Paul Winfield, Madge Sinclair
rows.extract: Conrack is a 1974 American drama film based on the 1972 autobiographical book The Water Is Wide by Pat Conroy, directed by Martin Ritt and starring Jon Voight in the title role, alongside Paul Winfield, Madge Sinclair, Hume Cronyn and Antonio Fargas. The film was released by 20th Century Fox on Marc

rows.title: The Conversation
rows.cast: Gene Hackman, John Cazale, Cindy Williams, Frederic Forrest, Harrison Ford
rows.extract: The Conversation is a 1974 American mystery thriller film written, produced, and directed by Francis Ford Coppola and starring Gene Hackman, John Cazale, Allen Garfield, Cindy Williams, Frederic Forrest, Harrison Ford, Teri Garr, and Robert Duvall. The film revolves around a surveillance expert and

rows.title: Crazy Joe
rows.cast: Peter Boyle, Paula Prentiss, Fred Williamson, Eli Wallach, Rip Torn
rows.extract: Crazy Joe is a 1974 crime film directed by Carlo Lizzani and produced by Dino De Laurentiis. The Italian-American co-production is a fictionalized retelling of the murder of Joseph "Crazy Joe" Gallo, a mobster who was gunned down on April 7, 1972, at a restaurant in Little Italy. The screenplay by L

rows.title: The Crazy World of Julius Vrooder
rows.cast: Timothy Bottoms, Barbara Hershey, Albert Salmi, George Marshall
rows.extract: The Crazy World of Julius Vrooder is a 1974 film from Playboy Enterprises directed by Arthur Hiller and produced by Hugh Hefner. This was the final film for actor George Marshall.

rows.title: Cry Panic
rows.cast: John Forsythe, Earl Holliman, Ralph Meeker, Norman Alden, Claudia McNeil
rows.extract: Cry Panic is a 1974 American made-for-television mystery film directed by James Goldstone and starring John Forsythe, Earl Holliman, Ralph Meeker, Norman Alden, Claudia McNeil and Anne Francis. The film premiered as the ABC Movie of the Week on February 6, 1974 and was co-produced by Aaron Spelling

rows.title: Daisy Miller
rows.cast: Cybill Shepherd, Cloris Leachman, Mildred Natwick
rows.extract: Daisy Miller is a 1974 American drama film produced and directed by Peter Bogdanovich, and starring Cybill Shepherd in the title role. rows.title: Dark Star
rows.cast: Dan O'Bannon, Brian Narelle, Cal Kuniholm, Dre Pahich, Nick Castle

rows.title: Death Cruise
rows.cast: Richard Long, Polly Bergen, Edward Albert, Kate Jackson, Celeste Holm
rows.extract: Death Cruise is a 1974 American made-for-television mystery film starring Richard Long, Polly Bergen, Edward Albert, Kate Jackson, Celeste Holm, Tom Bosley, Michael Constantine and Cesare Danova. It was directed by Ralph Senensky and aired as the ABC Movie of the Week on October 30, 1974.

rows.title: The Death Squad
rows.cast: Robert Forster, Michelle Philips, Claude Akins, Mark Goddard, Melvyn Douglas
rows.extract: The Death Squad is a 1974 American made-for-television crime drama film directed by Harry Falk and starring Robert Forster, Michelle Phillips, Claude Akins, Mark Goddard and Melvyn Douglas.

rows.title: Death Wish
rows.cast: Charles Bronson, Vincent Gardenia, Hope Lange, Stuart Margolin
rows.extract: Death Wish is a 1974 American neo-noir vigilante action thriller film loosely based on the 1972 novel of the same title by Brian Garfield. Directed by Michael Winner, the film stars Charles Bronson as Paul Kersey, an architect who becomes a vigilante after his wife and daughter are attacked during a

rows.title: Dirty Mary, Crazy Larry
rows.cast: Susan George, Peter Fonda, Vic Morrow
rows.extract: Dirty Mary, Crazy Larry is a 1974 American road crime drama film based on the 1963 Richard Unekis novel titled The Chase. Directed by John Hough, the film stars Peter Fonda, Susan George, Adam Roarke, and Vic Morrow. Although Jimmie Haskell is credited with writing the music score, the soundtrack co

rows.title: Dirty O'Neil
rows.cast: Morgan Paull, Art Metrano, Pat Anderson
rows.extract: Dirty O'Neil is a 1974 American film directed by Leon Capetanos and Lewis Teague.

rows.title: The Dove
rows.cast: Joseph Bottoms, Dabney Coleman, Deborah Raffin
rows.extract: The Dove is a 1974 American biographical film directed by Charles Jarrott. The picture was produced by Gregory Peck, the third and last feature film he would produce.

rows.title: Dynamite Brothers
rows.cast: Timothy Brown, Alan Tang, Aldo Ray
rows.extract: Dynamite Brothers, also known by its alternate title East Meets Watts, is a 1974 martial arts and blaxploitation film.

rows.title: Earthquake
rows.cast: Charlton Heston, Ava Gardner, Richard Roundtree, George Kennedy, Geneviève Bujold
rows.extract: Earthquake is a 1974 American ensemble disaster drama film directed and produced by Mark Robson and starring Charlton Heston and Ava Gardner. The plot concerns the struggle for survival after a catastrophic earthquake destroys most of the city of Los Angeles, California.

rows.title: The Education of Sonny Carson
rows.cast: Don Gordon, Joyce Walker, Paul Benjamin
rows.extract: The Education of Sonny Carson is a 1974 American blaxploitation drama film based on the best-selling autobiography of Sonny Carson. The film was directed by The Mack director Michael Campus, and starring Rony Clanton, Don Gordon, Joyce Walker, Paul Benjamin, and Mary Alice.

rows.title: Flesh Gordon
rows.cast: William Dennis Hunt, John Hoyt, Candy Samples
rows.extract: Flesh Gordon is a 1974 American sex comedy feature film serving as a spoof of Universal Pictures's first Flash Gordon serial films from the 1930s. The film was produced by Walter R. Cichy, Bill Osco, and Howard Ziehm. It was co-directed by Ziehm and Michael Benveniste, who also wrote the screenplay.

rows.title: For Pete's Sake
rows.cast: Barbra Streisand, Michael Sarrazin, Estelle Parsons
rows.extract: For Pete's Sake is a 1974 American screwball comedy film starring Barbra Streisand and directed by Peter Yates. The screenplay by Stanley Shapiro and Maurice Richlin chronicles the misadventures of a Brooklyn housewife. In 1977, it was used as the basis for the Hindi film Aap Ki Khatir.

rows.title: Foxy Brown
rows.cast: Pam Grier, Antonio Fargas, Terry Carter
rows.extract: Foxy Brown is a 1974 American blaxploitation film written and directed by Jack Hill. It stars Pam Grier as the title character who takes on a gang of white drug dealers who murdered her boyfriend. The film was released by American International Pictures as a double feature with Truck Turner. The fil

rows.title: Freebie and the Bean
rows.cast: Alan Arkin, James Caan, Loretta Swit
rows.extract: Freebie and the Bean is a 1974 American buddy cop black comedy action film directed by Richard Rush and starring James Caan, Alan Arkin, Loretta Swit and Valerie Harper. The film follows two off-beat police detectives who wreak havoc in San Francisco attempting to bring down an organized crime boss.

rows.title: The Front Page
rows.cast: Jack Lemmon, Walter Matthau, Susan Sarandon, Carol Burnett
rows.extract: The Front Page is a 1974 American black comedy-drama film directed by Billy Wilder, and starring Jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau. The screenplay by Wilder and I.A.L. rows.title: The Gambler
rows.cast: James Caan, Lauren Hutton, Paul Sorvino
rows.extract:
The Gambler is a 1974 American crime drama film written by James Toback and directed by Karel Reisz. It stars James Caan, Paul Sorvino and Lauren Hutton. 
Caan's performance was widely lauded and was nominated for a Golden Globe.

rows.title: 'Gator Bait
rows.cast: Claudia Jennings, Bill Thurman
rows.extract: 'Gator Bait is a 1974 film written, produced, and directed by Beverly Sebastian and Ferd Sebastian.

rows.title: Ginger in the Morning
rows.cast: Fred Ward, Sissy Spacek, Monte Markham
rows.extract: Ginger in the Morning is a 1974 comedy-drama-romance film starring Sissy Spacek as a hitchhiker. It was only the third theatrical film for Spacek, and the first American film appearance of Fred Ward.

rows.title: The Girl from Petrovka
rows.cast: Goldie Hawn, Hal Holbrook, Anthony Hopkins
rows.extract: The Girl from Petrovka is a 1974 American comedy-drama film starring Goldie Hawn and Hal Holbrook, based on the novel by George Feifer. rows.extract: The Godfather Part II is a 1974 American epic crime film produced and directed by Francis Ford Coppola. rows.title: Golden Needles
rows.cast: Joe Don Baker, Elizabeth Ashley, Ann Sothern, Jim Kelly, Burgess Meredith
rows.extract: Golden Needles is a 1974 American action/adventure film starring Joe Don Baker, Elizabeth Ashley, Ann Sothern, Jim Kelly, Burgess Meredith, and Roy Chiao. The film was directed by Robert Clouse and shot on location in Hong Kong.

rows.title: Gone in 60 Seconds
rows.cast: H. B. Halicki, Gary Bettenhausen, Parnelli Jones
rows.extract: Gone in 60 Seconds is a 1974 American action film written, directed, produced by, and starring H. B. Halicki. rows.title: The Gravy Train
rows.cast: Stacy Keach, Margot Kidder, Frederic Forrest
rows.extract: The Gravy Train, also commonly known as The Dion Brothers, is a 1974 American crime-comedy film directed by Jack Starrett, written by Terrence Malick and Bill Kerby, and starring Stacy Keach and Frederic Forrest.

rows.title: The Great Gatsby
rows.cast: Robert Redford, Mia Farrow, Sam Waterston, Bruce Dern, Karen Black
rows.extract: The Great Gatsby is a 1974 American romantic drama film based on the 1925 novel of the same name by F. Scott Fitzgerald. rows.title: The Groove Tube
rows.cast: Chevy Chase, Richard Belzer, Jennifer Welles
rows.extract: The Groove Tube is a 1974 American independent comedy film written and produced by Ken Shapiro and starring Shapiro, Richard Belzer and Chevy Chase. It features the song "Move On Up" by Curtis Mayfield in its opening scene.

rows.title: Hangup
rows.cast: William Elliott, Cliff Potts, Marki Bey
rows.extract: Hangup, also called  Hang Up and later released under the name Super Dude, is a 1974 film directed by Henry Hathaway. It stars William Elliott and Marki Bey. This was the last film directed by Hathaway.

rows.title: Harry and Tonto
rows.cast: Art Carney, Ellen Burstyn, Larry Hagman
rows.extract: Harry and Tonto is a 1974 road movie written by Paul Mazursky and Josh Greenfeld and directed by Mazursky. It features Art Carney as Harry in an Oscar-winning performance. Tonto is his pet cat.

rows.title: Heatwave!
rows.cast: Ben Murphy, Bonnie Bedelia, David Huddleston, Lew Ayres, Dana Elcar
rows.extract: Heatwave! is an American disaster movie that was broadcast on the ABC television network on January 26, 1974. It was an ABC Movie of the Week. Its running time was 90 minutes. The film was directed by Jerry Jameson, produced by Herbert F. Solow and Harve Bennett.

rows.title: Herbie Rides Again
rows.cast: Helen Hayes, Ken Berry, Stefanie Powers, Keenan Wynn
rows.extract: Herbie Rides Again is a 1974 American comedy film directed by Robert Stevenson from a screenplay by Bill Walsh, based on a story by Gordon Buford. rows.title: Homebodies
rows.cast: Peter Brocco, Frances Fuller, William Hansen
rows.extract: Homebodies is a 1974 comedy horror film directed by Larry Yust. The film features a cast of veteran actors, including Ian Wolfe, Ruth McDevitt, Peter Brocco, and Douglas Fowley. The film centers on elderly residents resorting to murder to protect their condemned building.

rows.title: The House on Skull Mountain
rows.cast: Victor French, Janee Michelle, Mike Evans
rows.extract: The House on Skull Mountain is a 1974 horror film directed by Ron Honthaner. After Pauline Christophe, the sole heir for the mansion on Skull Mountain dies, four of her family members are called to hear her will. Upon arrival, each of the guests is stalked by a skeleton in a robe.

rows.title: How to Seduce a Woman
rows.cast: Angel Tompkins, Alexandra Hay, Judith McConnell
rows.extract: How to Seduce a Woman is a 1974 American comedy film, directed by Charles Martin. It stars Angus Duncan, Angel Tompkins, and Alexandra Hay, and was released in late January 1974.

rows.title: Huckleberry Finn
rows.cast: Jeff East, Paul Winfield, David Wayne, Arthur O'Connell, Harvey Korman
rows.extract: Huckleberry Finn is a 1974 musical film version of Mark Twain's 1884 novel The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.

rows.title: Hurricane
rows.cast: Larry Hagman, Martin Milner, Jessica Walter, Barry Sullivan, Michael Learned
rows.extract: Hurricane is a 1974 American TV film. It was an ABC Movie of the Week.

rows.title: The Island at the Top of the World
rows.cast: David Hartman, Mako
rows.extract: The Island at the Top of the World is a 1974 American live-action lost world fantasy adventure film directed by Robert Stevenson and produced by Winston Hibler. It was released by Walt Disney Productions, distributed by Buena Vista Distribution and starring Donald Sinden and David Hartman.

rows.title: It's Alive
rows.cast: John P. Ryan, Sharon Farrell, Guy Stockwell
rows.extract: It's Alive is a 1974 American science fiction horror film written, produced, and directed by Larry Cohen. It stars John P. rows.title: Juggernaut
rows.cast: Richard Harris, Omar Sharif, Freddie Jones
rows.extract: Juggernaut is a 1974 British crime suspense film starring Richard Harris, Omar Sharif, and Anthony Hopkins. rows.title: Killdozer!
rows.cast: Clint Walker, Carl Betz, Neville Brand, Robert Urich
rows.extract: Killdozer! is a 1974 made for TV science-fiction horror movie, adapted from a 1944 novella of the same name by Theodore Sturgeon. A comic book adaptation appeared the same year, in Marvel Comics' Worlds Unknown #6. The film has since gained a cult following.

rows.title: The Klansman
rows.cast: Lee Marvin, Richard Burton, Cameron Mitchell, Linda Evans, O. J. Simpson
rows.extract: The Klansman is a 1974 American drama film based on the 1967 book of the same name by William Bradford Huie. It was directed by Terence Young and starred Lee Marvin, Richard Burton, O. J. Simpson, Lola Falana and Linda Evans. The film is in the public domain.

rows.title: Knife for the Ladies
rows.cast: Jack Elam, Ruth Roman, Gene Evans
rows.extract: Knife for the Ladies is a 1974 American Western horror film directed by Larry G. Spangler and starring Jack Elam, Ruth Roman and Gene Evans. It was the first production from the company Bryanston Pictures.

rows.title: Law and Disorder
rows.cast: Carroll O'Connor, Ernest Borgnine, Ann Wedgeworth, Karen Black
rows.extract: Law and Disorder is a 1974 American comedy-drama film directed by Ivan Passer, starring Carroll O'Connor, Ernest Borgnine, Ann Wedgeworth and Karen Black.

rows.cast: Peter Haskell, Slim Pickens, Keenan Wynn

rows.cast: Dustin Hoffman, Valerie Perrine, Jan Miner
rows.extract: Lenny is a 1974 American biographical drama film about the comedian Lenny Bruce, starring Dustin Hoffman and directed by Bob Fosse. The screenplay by Julian Barry is based on his play of the same name.

rows.extract: The Little Prince is a 1974 British-American sci-fi fantasy-musical film with screenplay and lyrics by Alan Jay Lerner, music by Frederick Loewe, arranged and orchestrated by Angela Morley. rows.cast: Perry King, Henry Winkler, Sylvester Stallone, Susan Blakely

rows.title: Lost in the Stars
rows.cast: Brock Peters, Melba Moore, Clifton Davis
rows.extract: Lost in the Stars is the 1974 film version of the Kurt Weill-Maxwell Anderson musical adaptation of the Alan Paton novel Cry, the Beloved Country. The film was produced and released as part of the American Film Theatre, which adapted theatrical works for a subscription-driven cinema series.

rows.title: Lovin' Molly
rows.cast: Blythe Danner, Anthony Perkins, Beau Bridges
rows.extract: Lovin' Molly is a 1974 American drama film directed by Sidney Lumet and starring Anthony Perkins, Beau Bridges, Blythe Danner in the title role, Ed Binns, and Susan Sarandon.
